domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the taxation of companies, including self-assessment, distributions, and group structures. It represents 35% of the exam content, focusing on the application of tax rules to corporate entities and their financial activities during the assessment.

This domain addresses VAT rules and procedures, accounting for 20% of the exam. It focuses on the mechanics of VAT, including registration, taxable supplies, and the administration of the tax system for businesses within the current regulatory framework.

Focusing on owner-managed businesses, this domain accounts for 20% of the exam. It covers the interaction between business income and personal tax liabilities, including National Insurance contributions for business owners operating within the professional tax environment.

This domain covers Capital Gains Tax for individuals and companies, representing 15% of the exam. It involves calculating gains and losses and applying relevant reliefs and exemptions in a business context to ensure accurate tax reporting and compliance.

This domain accounts for 10% of the exam and covers Stamp Taxes and other miscellaneous taxes. It requires knowledge of when these taxes apply to business transactions and property dealings to maintain full compliance with current legislation.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: The exam is a written paper lasting 210 minutes. Candidates must manage their time effectively across the five domains. Ensure you have your identification and required materials ready for the session, which costs approximately £300–£500 per sitting.

faq.answer_text: To successfully pass the ACA Professional Level: Business Planning: Taxation exam, candidates must achieve a score of 55. This threshold is mandatory for all candidates seeking to demonstrate their technical competency in the subject matter before the scheduled retirement date.

The exam is a written paper with a total duration of 210 minutes. Candidates should plan their time carefully to address all five domains within this period, ensuring that each section receives adequate attention to meet the required passing standard.

methodology.summary: This page was built by aggregating official ICAEW certification documentation and HMRC manuals to provide a summary of the exam domains, structure, and retirement status for all prospective candidates.

editorial.overview: The ACA Professional Level: Business Planning: Taxation exam, certified by ICAEW, covers five key tax domains. It evaluates technical knowledge across corporation tax, VAT, income tax, capital gains tax, and stamp taxes. This written paper is a component of the professional qualification, requiring candidates to demonstrate application of tax rules to business scenarios. The exam is scheduled for retirement on 2026-09-30, with the Fundamental Case Study serving as the official successor. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency across these areas to progress in their professional development journey.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official ICAEW study documentation to understand the tax rules and procedures. Practice applying these regulations to business scenarios, as the exam is a written paper. Ensure familiarity with the five domains, focusing on the 35% weight assigned to Corporation Tax. Candidates should prepare for the 210-minute duration and aim to meet the 55 passing score. Direct your future studies toward the Fundamental Case Study to ensure your certification path remains aligned with current ICAEW requirements.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is for professional-level candidates pursuing the ACA qualification. It is intended for those who have completed earlier stages and are ready to apply tax legislation to business planning and owner-managed entity scenarios.

exam_format: Computer-based (Certificate Level); Written paper (Professional and Advanced Level)
exam_name: ACA Professional Level: Business Planning: Taxation
exam_rules: Certificate Level: computer-based, closed-book, 1.5 hours per paper. Professional Level: written, 3.5 hours, tax tables provided for BPT. Advanced Level Case Study: written, 4 hours, open book (pre-seen material permitted). No personal notes or unauthorised materials.
id_requirements: Valid government-issued photo ID. ICAEW student registration number required for booking. Name must match ICAEW registration.

lifecycle.summary: ICAEW retires BPT on 2026-09-30. Fundamental Case Study is the named replacement path.

official_study_resources.notes: Official ICAEW study manuals, question banks, and mock exams available via ICAEW's online learning platform (VITAL).
official_study_resources.title: ICAEW Learning Materials (ICAEW VITAL)

prerequisites.description: ACA Certificate Level must be completed before attempting Professional Level papers.

renewal_options: ACA qualification does not expire. ICAEW members must complete a minimum of 40 CPD hours per year to maintain membership and practising certificate. Ongoing CPD is mandatory for practising members.

retake_policy.notes: Exams are offered in March/June/September/December windows. Students may attempt each paper multiple times; full fee required for each attempt. No maximum attempt limit, but progress reviews apply under training contract rules.

testing_centers.notes: Certificate Level papers are computer-based, booked at Pearson VUE test centres. Professional and Advanced Level papers are written (paper-based) examinations, sat in ICAEW-approved examination centres worldwide.
